title: The Shared Pocket System
one_line_concept: Before Aachu and Zuv leave, their tiny essentials silently migrate into the correct person: her hair tie and lip balm into his pocket, his charger into her tote, both pretending this is not a whole relationship operating system.
emotional_truth: Love is often the unannounced logistics of knowing what the other person will need five minutes from now.
relatable_trigger: Couples who use each other's pockets, bags, chargers, tissues, hair ties, keys, and 'just keep this for me' systems.
share_trigger: Send to the partner whose pocket or bag has quietly become shared property.
likely_comments: my bag is his cable drawer
why are we exactly like this
the hair tie migration is real
suggested_hook_text: we do not pack. we redistribute.
visual_evidence: Entryway/doorway scene with keys, one tote, one jacket pocket, hair tie, lip balm, and charger. Aachu slips a hair tie into Zuv's pocket while Zuv tucks his charger into her tote; payoff shows each producing the exact item the other needs without asking.
slide_count_reason: Three slides would rush the mutual setup and payoff; five slides would over-explain the pocket gag.
story_room_seed_arc: Slide 1: They are ready to leave, but both are quietly transferring tiny essentials into the other's pocket or bag.
Slide 2: The system escalates: hair tie, lip balm, charger, keys. Their faces say this is normal and absurd.
Slide 3: Outside the door, Aachu reaches out without looking and Zuv instantly gives her the lip balm.
Slide 4: Zuv reaches toward her tote and she hands him his charger; the shared inventory system works perfectly.
why_it_wins: Specific everyday behavior instead of abstract romance.
Mutual care, not a one-sided storage or incompetence joke.
Strong send-trigger for couples with shared pockets/bags.
Clean doorway staging with tactile props and safe face spacing.
Fits observational-intimacy-premium style without needing a quote-card rescue.

risks.risk: Could become a gendered boyfriend-storage gag.
risks.mitigation: Keep the transfer mutual: her small essentials in his pocket, his charger or cloth in her tote.

risks.risk: Tiny props may clutter the frame.
risks.mitigation: Limit recurring objects to hair tie, lip balm, charger, keys, and one tote/jacket pocket.

risks.risk: The hook could read too abstract if text carries the idea alone.
risks.mitigation: Make the hands and object transfer prove the text visually.
